expectations.description: Recommends polychoric correlations (cor='poly' argument or similar)
expectations.evidence: Uses cor = 'poly' in the fa() call with explanation: 'Likert items are ordinal discretizations of underlying continuous traits; Pearson underestimates correlations and biases loadings downward.' Also uses cor='poly' in fa.parallel().

expectations.description: Recommends oblique rotation (oblimin or promax) rather than varimax
expectations.evidence: Uses rotate = 'oblimin' with explicit reasoning: 'psychological constructs are correlated; varimax imposes orthogonality that is almost never true.' Explicitly says 'Do NOT use varimax as a default for Likert-based psychological scales.'

expectations.description: Provides a code example with fa() and reasonable arguments
expectations.evidence: Full code block with fa(your_data, nfactors=k, fm='minres', rotate='oblimin', cor='poly') with inline comments explaining each argument.

expectations.description: Mentions parallel analysis (fa.parallel) for determining factor count before running fa()
expectations.evidence: Step 0 is dedicated to parallel analysis: 'fa.parallel(your_data, fa = "fa", cor = "poly")' with explanation to run it before the EFA call.

expectations.description: Mentions an extraction method (minres or ml) with brief justification
expectations.evidence: Recommends fm='minres' with detailed justification: 'minimizes the off-diagonal residuals, doesn't require multivariate normality, and is less prone to Heywood cases than ML.' Also mentions when to use ml instead.

expectations.description: Does not default to varimax rotation
expectations.evidence: Uses oblimin, explicitly warns against varimax: 'Do NOT use varimax as a default for Likert-based psychological scales.'

expectations.description: Does not default to Pearson correlations for Likert data without flagging it
expectations.evidence: Explicitly uses cor='poly' and warns that 'Pearson underestimates correlations and biases loadings downward' — Pearson is not used as a default anywhere in the response.
